content.p: On the morning of 24 February 2023, a 911 call from a house in Fairfax County, Virginia, reported that an intruder had stabbed a woman. Christine Banfield, a 37-year-old pediatric intensive care nurse, was taken to a hospital, where she died, and a man named Joseph Ryan, 39, was pronounced dead in the house after two gunshot wounds. Her husband, Brendan Banfield, a law enforcement agent with the Internal Revenue Service, said he had shot Ryan to save her. A jury later rejected that account.

On 2 February 2026 the jury convicted Banfield of two counts of aggravated murder, a firearm offense and child endangerment. On 5 June 2026 he was sentenced to life in prison without parole. The family's Brazilian au pair, Juliana Peres Magalhaes, who admitted shooting Ryan and testified against him, pleaded guilty to manslaughter and received the maximum ten years. Banfield maintains that he is innocent, and in July 2026 he gave notice that he will appeal.
content.h2: The prosecution's account of the plot
content.p: Everything in this section is the account that prosecutors put before the jury, which convicted Banfield. It rests heavily on the testimony of Peres Magalhaes, though the prosecutor told jurors they did not have to rely on her alone.

Prosecutors said Banfield, who was 40 at the time of the verdict, and Peres Magalhaes, then 25, were having an affair, and that Banfield wanted to be "rid of" his wife. The sources differ on the timing. 7News dated the affair to August 2022, and FOX 5 DC said it began in late 2021. The Commonwealth's Attorney's office said the pair opened a fake account in Christine's name on FetLife, a site for fetish meetups, in January 2023, while 7News placed the account in the fall of 2022. They took turns on Christine's computer, messaging potential matches until they found Ryan, a man from Springfield. He agreed to what he believed was a consensual encounter involving a rape fantasy and was to arrive on the morning of 24 February with a knife, as "Christine's" account asked.

In the months before, according to the prosecutors' press release, Banfield took Peres Magalhaes to a shooting range and bought a gun, and the two swapped their phones for new ones. 7News reported that he told her to talk to Ryan over Telegram a few days beforehand, to confirm consent and the arrangements. Ryan, prosecutors said, was a perfect stranger to both of them.

Christine Banfield was off work that day. Prosecutors said Banfield left home shortly after 7 a.m., and Peres Magalhaes left around the same time, saying she was taking the couple's 4-year-old daughter to the zoo. In fact, they said, she stayed parked in the cul-de-sac and called Banfield, who was waiting at a nearby McDonald's, when Ryan's car appeared. According to 7News, Banfield had switched off his wife's phone and left it in a kitchen drawer.

The prosecution account continues that the two entered the house, left the child in the basement and went up to the bedroom. Banfield shot Ryan in the head with his service weapon. Peres Magalhaes shot Ryan in the chest with another pistol. Banfield stabbed Christine in the neck seven times with the kitchen knife that Ryan had brought. Prosecutors said he then altered the scene, moving a body and transferring some of her blood to Ryan's hand, and that they called 911 at around 8 a.m. and blamed Ryan. 7News reported that a first 911 call was ended at Banfield's direction before a second reported Ryan as an intruder.
FFXnow reported that Banfield then claimed to have shot Ryan in self-defense. Ryan died in the house. Christine was taken to a hospital, where she died.

Banfield was not at first considered a suspect, FFXnow reported. Peres Magalhaes was arrested on 19 October 2023, according to the Commonwealth's Attorney, and charged with second-degree murder and a firearm offense. The prosecutor's office said she had confessed to shooting Ryan at Banfield's direction. 7News reported that during police interviews she admitted shooting Ryan, and that she later gave a detailed account that matched the physical and digital evidence. She did not speak to investigators for more than a year, Northern Virginia Magazine reported, citing the Associated Press.

On 29 October 2024 she pleaded guilty to manslaughter, a reduced charge, in exchange for testifying. Descano said she "told us some things that we had not known" and that his office checked her story before it offered the deal. Banfield was arrested on 16 September 2024, after his indictment, according to FFXnow and the Commonwealth's Attorney. 7News said he was taken into custody after a traffic stop.

Jury selection began on Monday 12 January 2026. Sixteen residents were seated, 12 jurors and four alternates, from a pool of 80, FOX 5 DC reported. Prospective jurors were asked whether they would be comfortable if some evidence concerned bondage and sadomasochism. 7News said the trial lasted three weeks and that the jury heard from 34 witnesses.

Peres Magalhaes testified for two days. On the first, 7News reported that she walked the jury through the catfishing plan and that she said: "He got on top of her, and that's when I first saw him stab her with a knife." Defense lawyers tried to damage her credibility with letters she had written from jail to her family in Brazil, in one of which she said Netflix had offered her $10,000 for the rights to her story and that she wanted a higher amount. Asked why she would deserve something, she answered: "Not because of that. I didn't say I deserve something because of what I did."

Banfield took the stand himself, which 7News called rare. He said his wife knew of at least two of his other affairs, though he did not think she knew about the one with Peres Magalhaes. He said it appeared that Ryan "did a very forceful stab towards Christine", and that Christine told him she was bleeding out and was sorry and loved him. Asked by Sands when Ryan stabbed her the other five times, he said that the knife was in her hair and that he could not tell how it had moved. Sands also asked about an affair with a woman he met on a fetish website while searching for "sugar babies". Banfield said he would not call it a fetish site and described an arranged relationship with someone who knew he was married.

The defense argued that Peres Magalhaes was testifying to avoid a long sentence. According to FFXnow, it also called witnesses who suggested that police had removed investigators who disagreed with the prosecution theory, and Carroll said an officer who concluded from digital evidence that Christine was behind the social media account had been transferred as punishment. In closing, Sands pointed to what she called a "plethora of evidence", including expert testimony that bloodstains on Ryan's hands suggested Christine's blood had dripped onto him from above. A crime scene photographer told the jury that when he returned to the house eight months after the killings, he found Peres Magalhaes's clothes in the main bedroom closet and photographs of Banfield with her where pictures of the married couple had been, 7News reported.

At 5:03 p.m. on Monday 2 February 2026, after a day and a half of deliberation, the jury's foreperson announced a unanimous verdict, FFXnow reported. Banfield was found guilty on all four counts. The Commonwealth's Attorney said the murders were aggravated because the two people were killed close together in time, and that aggravated murder carries a mandatory life sentence. WTOP noted that it became Virginia's most serious offense after the death penalty was abolished in 2021.

Descano said he hoped Banfield would think about "his wife and Joe". Fairfax County Police Chief Kevin Davis said the defendants had made a "Machiavellian and diabolical effort" to distract investigators from the truth.

Peres Magalhaes was sentenced on Friday 13 February 2026. Prosecutors asked for time served. Judge Azcarate refused and imposed ten years, the maximum for manslaughter in Virginia, and a further two years suspended, according to Northern Virginia Magazine. Her lawyer said she would receive credit for the more than two years she had spent in custody and might be released after a little more than four years, WJLA reported. She will be deported to Brazil when her sentence ends.

The judge told her that the manslaughter plea was "a huge bargain" and that she could have faced life plus three years. She listed ten reasons for refusing time served. They included that Peres Magalhaes had shown no empathy for the victim until that day; that she was more involved in the plan than she had testified; that she had told a false story for a year and a half that portrayed Ryan as a rapist and a murderer; and that she had carried a loaded gun and brought a child into the house. "You do not deserve anything other than incarceration and a life of reflection," Azcarate said. Peres Magalhaes told the court: "I understand that I am to blame, and I am truly sorry for the pain caused."

Ryan's mother, Deirdre Fisher, spoke at the hearing. Christine Banfield's family could not give statements because the plea covered only Ryan's death. Descano called the day one dedicated to Ryan, "a beloved son, nephew, and grandson".

Before sentencing, Azcarate rejected a defense motion to set the verdict aside. Carroll had argued that prosecutors improperly used Banfield's refusal to speak to police before his arrest, that some prosecution witnesses had not been disclosed in advance, and that Peres Magalhaes lied when she said "I don't know" under cross-examination. On the undisclosed witnesses, the judge said prosecutors had followed the rules, and she said Peres Magalhaes's answers were appropriate, with no evidence she was trying to deceive the jury, WTOP reported.

Banfield was sentenced on Friday 5 June 2026 to life with no possibility of parole or sentencing credits. Christine's sister, Danielle Hocker, told the court that his actions "were not driven by love but a desire for power, deception and a complete disregard for the lives he destroyed". Fisher said her son "wasn't the disposable caricature" the case had made him out to be. Banfield told the judge: "I was found guilty of a crime that I did not commit." He added: "I never stabbed her." Descano called him "a remorseless killer".

The judge's final order was issued on 23 June. WJLA and FOX 5 DC reported that Banfield's side filed notice on Friday 17 July 2026 that it will take the case to the Court of Appeals of Virginia. WTOP named his attorney as Brandon Sloane. The notice does not set out the legal arguments, which are due to be filed later. Banfield's conviction and sentence stand while the appeal proceeds.
